title: Hilib Ari Karis
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Bone-in goat meat slow-boiled with whole spices until falling-off-the-bone tender, then finished with a quick fry in ghee for a dish that's both a celebration centerpiece and everyday staple.
longDesc: This two-stage technique - a long, gentle boil followed by a final fry - is common across Somali meat cookery, the boiling stage tenderizing tougher cuts while the finishing fry in ghee develops a deeply savory crust and rich aroma just before serving.
ingredients: 1.2 kg (2.6 lb) bone-in goat meat, cut into pieces
steps: Place the goat meat in a large pot with the quartered onion, cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaves, ginger, and whole garlic cloves.
Cover generously with water and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook, covered, for 1-1.5 hours, until the meat is very tender.
Remove the meat from the broth (reserving the broth for another use, such as maraq) and pat dry.
Melt the ghee in a large skillet and saute the sliced onion until golden.
Add the boiled goat pieces and fry for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until deeply browned and slightly crisp on the edges.
Season with salt, finish with fresh cilantro, and serve hot.
chefTips: The initial long boil is essential for tenderizing the goat meat before the finishing fry.
Do not discard the flavorful cooking broth - it makes an excellent base for maraq or another soup.
The final fry in ghee is what gives this dish its rich aroma and deeply savory crust.
commonMistakes: Rushing the initial boil, which leaves the meat tough rather than properly tender.
Skipping the final fry, missing the flavorful crust and aroma this step develops.
Discarding the cooking broth, wasting a flavorful base that could be used elsewhere.
reheating: Reheat gently in a pan with a little extra ghee.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein and iron from the goat meat.
culturalNote: This two-stage boil-then-fry technique is common across Somali meat cookery, valued both as an everyday preparation and as a centerpiece for larger family gatherings.
